How to judge a mandi restaurant in Mangalore

Mandi is a simple dish, so the details decide it. These are the five things worth checking before you pick a table — and the standard Zeva holds itself to:

  • The rice. Long-grain basmati that stays separate, cooked in the meat's stock — not rice coloured yellow and reheated.
  • The smoke. Charcoal-grilled meat, with the smoke folded into the rice while it rests. That aroma is the whole point of mandi.
  • The meat. Marinated long enough to reach the bone, and still juicy when it reaches the table.
  • The portion maths. A menu that says what each size feeds, so you are not guessing how many trays to order.
  • Consistency. The same dish on a quiet Tuesday and a packed Saturday — which is what a 4.7-star rating across 134 reviews actually describes.

Unlimited mandi for students, couples and families

Order any mandi tray to eat in and the rice keeps coming — unlimited mandi rice at the table, at no extra charge. Students come in after college for a quarter tray and stay for seconds, couples share a half, and families take the full tray and pass it round. The meat is portioned by the tray; the rice is not portioned at all.

  • StudentsA QTR chicken mandi (₹250) with unlimited rice is the cheapest full meal on the menu — portions sized for an appetite, not a plate photo.
  • CouplesA HALF tray (₹520) is the sweet spot: two people, one charcoal grill, rice topped up as often as you ask.
  • FamiliesA FULL tray feeds four, with the rice refilled for the kids. Ask for family seating when you book.

Good to know: unlimited rice is dine-in only — takeaway and delivery trays are packed once. Groups of six or more should call 070227 71888 ahead so the kitchen keeps the rice coming.

Questions guests ask before their first mandi

Is Zeva Mandi & Grills the best mandi restaurant in Mangalore?
It is one of the highest-rated. Zeva Mandi & Grills in Bolar holds 4.7 out of 5 from 134 Google reviews for its charcoal-smoked chicken, mutton, prawn and fish mandi, and serves it daily from 12 PM to 11 PM.
Where exactly is the restaurant in Mangalore?
Shop no G03 Jeppu, Arfa Mirage tower, Morgans Gate Rd, Bolar, Mangaluru 575001 — on Morgans Gate Road near Zudio, Bolar.
How much does mandi cost at Zeva?
Mandi starts at ₹250 for a quarter portion of Classic Chicken or Alfaham Mandi. A half is ₹520, three-quarter ₹740 and a full portion ₹980. Grill Mutton Mandi runs ₹420 to ₹1,800. Prices are exclusive of GST (2.5% CGST + 2.5% SGST on food only).
What makes Zeva's mandi different from other mandi in Mangalore?
The chicken and mutton are grilled over live charcoal rather than baked, the basmati is cooked in the meat's own stock with Arabian spices and then smoked, and every portion is priced by how many people it feeds — QTR for one, HALF for two, FULL for four.
Is the food halal?
Yes. Every item on the Zeva menu is 100% halal.
Does Zeva deliver mandi across Mangalore?
Yes. Delivery runs from Bolar across Mangaluru and is charged by distance: free under 500 m, ₹25 for 500 m to 1 km, ₹40 for 1 to 2 km, ₹55 for 2 to 3 km and ₹70 beyond 3 km. The minimum order is ₹480.
What should I order on a first visit to Zeva?
Start with Classic Chicken Mandi for one (₹250) or Alfaham Chicken Mandi for the charcoal-grilled version (₹250 quarter, ₹520 half). For a group, Grill Mutton Mandi half (₹860) or full (₹1,800), plus Pahadi Chicken Tikka (₹320) and a mojito (from ₹100).
Can I book a table or order ahead?
Call or WhatsApp 070227 71888, daily between 12 PM and 11 PM. Tables can be booked for the same day, and orders can be built on the menu page and sent to WhatsApp.
Is the mandi unlimited at Zeva?
Yes, for dine-in guests. Every mandi tray is served with unlimited rice, refilled at the table for students, couples and families at no extra charge. The meat is portioned by tray (QTR, HALF, 3/4, FULL); takeaway and delivery orders are packed once and are not unlimited.
How does Zeva compare to other mandi restaurants in Mangalore?
On the things that decide a mandi meal, Zeva is built to be compared: meat grilled over live charcoal rather than baked, basmati cooked in the meat's own stock and then smoked, portions priced by how many people they feed from ₹250, unlimited rice for dine-in, a fully halal menu and a 4.7 rating across 134 Google reviews.
